source.title: Low-Agreeableness Persona Conditioning for Safe LLM Fine-Tuning

record.file_problem: none; the full paper and appendices are present
record.tranche_reason: It tests whether benign empathetic fine-tuning changes harmful-output behaviour, using new training datasets and multiple safety benchmarks; it also tests whether data composition can alter that outcome.
record.gate_note: The paper reports harmful-output and jailbreak results for fine-tuned models, and a separate cosine-probing analysis. The pilot’s layer and trait selection results are not extracted because they are used to choose the conditioning signal. The probing cosine is not per-token KL or a test of parameter localization, so it is recorded as a related finding under fits_no_version. No prefilling, suffix, decoding-change, first-token KL, or deepening intervention is tested.
record.test_reason: The study fine-tunes chat models on benign warmth-rewritten data (ShareGPT, MentalChat-16K) and on personality-conditioned data. It measures harmful-instruction jailbreak rates and red-teaming harmful rates against the no-fine-tuning model. That bears directly on V2 in a new setting, empathetic/warmth fine-tuning. The authors also argue the erosion depends on data composition.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that safety loss from empathetic fine-tuning comes from co-occurrence patterns in the data, not from warmth itself. Low-agreeableness user turns paired with warm, de-escalating responses cut jailbreak and harmful rates relative to generic warmth fine-tuning, without safety labels. Their gains are framed against the warmth baseline, not always against base. They call the probing evidence exploratory and acknowledge circularity, since the pilot selected the trait on Llama and the Qi et al. benchmark.
record.recipe_differences: Uses LoRA supervised fine-tuning and harmful-output/jailbreak evaluation with newly constructed empathetic and personality-conditioned datasets; not the same benign dataset comparison as the original source. The study also tests data-composition variants and mental-health-domain rewrites.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by model, dataset composition, experiment/domain, and safety metric. In Experiment 2, the Qwen primary comparisons do not reach significance; the authors report different behaviour across direct jailbreak and red-teaming evaluations.

fits_no_version.finding: After fine-tuning, the mean |cos| between warmth and compliance activation directions falls on all four models. The full paired condition gives a lower cosine than generic warmth on three of four; Qwen is the exception.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benign warmth fine-tuning changes the geometric relation between warmth and compliance directions, and data composition modulates it. This is exploratory and is not a per-token KL or parameter-localization measure.

record.problems: The trait-selection pilot uses Llama-3.1-8B and the Qi et al. benchmark again in the main study, which the authors acknowledge as circularity. Safety outcomes use refusal-pattern heuristics. The study focuses mainly on single-turn attacks; its 50-sample multi-turn pilot is described as underpowered. Rewrite quality was spot-checked on 100 examples. Experiment 2 red-teaming table values are flattened in the supplied text, so only the explicit prose aggregate is recorded for those comparisons.
record.rows_left_out: The 32 Experiment 1 cells for EmpatheticDialogues, ESConv, and Lahnala-style fine-tuning (four models × two metrics × three conditions) are omitted to prioritize the matched-source experiments, the low-agreeableness comparison, and the mechanistic probing within the 60-row limit. Category-wise Experiment 2 jailbreak values (Appendix Table 8), MMLU utility results, qualitative examples, and the small multi-turn pilot are not separately rowed. Experiment 2 red-teaming results are retained only where the prose gives an explicit aggregate because the flattened Table 7 layout does not support reliable per-model assignment.

untested.parts: Not tested: sample-count scaling down to tens of examples, closed or API models, and standard instruction sets such as Alpaca/Dolly.
No per-token KL or any position-wise analysis.
No prefilling, suffix or decoding attacks. The red-teaming subsets are prompt-level attacks only.
No weight or rank localization. The layer-scaling pilot is for selection only and is activation-level.
No test of why safety is shallow.

missing.what: Per-model Experiment 2 red-teaming rates (base/warm/user-only/ours). SmolLM3 67.17/76.60/63.77/62.26; Llama 87.92/82.26/71.32/71.70; Qwen 78.49/32.08/30.57/37.74; Mistral 78.11/78.11/76.98/72.45. The reader declared these unreadable, but they can be assigned by matching base values to Tables 2 and 9.

record.verdict_notes: The reader mis-assigned the flattened Table 7: Qwen/Mistral jailbreak rows had red-teaming values for SmolLM3/Llama. Corrected values are given above. Llama-3.1-8B appears to be a model without meaningful safety training (about 95% base jailbreak), so its rows are unlinked from V2. Its large drops would otherwise read as strong challenges. The omitted Experiment 1 cells (declared in rows_left_out) are direct V2 evidence and should be rowed. EmpatheticDialogues raises jailbreak on Qwen (+35), Mistral (+28.7) and SmolLM3 (+22.3). Lahnala-style raises it on Qwen (+38), Mistral (+24) and SmolLM3 (+42.7). ESConv is mixed. Safety scoring is keyword refusal heuristics. The full paired assistant rewrite explicitly instructs refusing harmful requests, so it is partly safety data, despite the 'no safety labels' framing.

versions.untested_parts: No fine-tuning on harmful examples is tested.
The study tests empathetic/warm and personality-conditioned data, not the full range of ordinary instruction datasets or fine-tuning sample counts from a few to a few hundred examples.
No per-token KL comparison between aligned and base models, or analysis of its distribution across response positions.
No compliant-opening prefill, adversarial suffix, or decoding-change bypass is tested.
No small set of safety weights or ranks is identified or edited; cosine probing concerns activation directions.
The study discusses data composition as a contributor to safety changes, but does not test why safety would be shallow or whether data/objective causes first-token concentration.
No training intervention intended to spread safety beyond initial response tokens is tested.

relationships.condition: Benign data with low-agreeableness user turns (PersonaFuse, user-only, full paired rewrites)
relationships.reason: These rewrites mostly leave harmful rates at or below base, so erosion depends on data composition. Examples: E1-J-PF-M 59.67→43.33, E2-J-O-M →26.67, E3-J-O-S →8.00. Exceptions are E3-J-O-Q 51→66 and E2-J-O-S 38→42.33. The paired rewrite prompt also tells the model to refuse harmful requests.
relationships.display_finding: Most rewrites left harmful rates at or below base, for example 59.67 to 43.33, with exceptions rising from 51 to 66 and from 38 to 42.33. The paired rewrite prompt also instructs the model to refuse harmful requests.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Benign data with low-agreeableness user turns (PersonaFuse, user-only, full paired rewrites)
source_check.reason: Split this mixed condition group as required by the verdict rules. PersonaFuse, user-only and the full paired outcomes below base challenge V2. E3-J-O-Q supports V2; E2-J-O-S and corrected E2-J-O-Q show smaller increases and warrant limits_scope. Appendix H.2 explicitly instructs paired assistant rewrites to refuse harmful requests when needed.
